headline: The New York Times reports that citizen science groups are struggling with a rise in low-quality AI-generated material.
score_reason: Lowered by 1: only the headline is known, so the scale of the problem is unverified.
importance_line: Research that relies on volunteer contributions could be weakened by a flood of machine-made submissions, which matters to scientists, volunteers and the public who rely on the findings, though how large the problem is remains unclear.
summary: The New York Times reports on 16 Oct 2026 that citizen science groups, which rely on volunteers to collect or sort scientific data, are grappling with the rise of what it calls A.I. slop, meaning low-quality material made with AI.
notes: Headline only; the NYT page returned 403 and no reliable second outlet carries the story.
